summary: For n=4, independent one-interval cap-one inputs and a symmetric matrix with distinct eigenvalues {1,2,-2,3}, the full output obeys ||p_Q||_infinity<=pi/sqrt(3), yet for the spectral split Q=Q3+Q' the conditional density at the ordinary positive-density value Q'=6 has p_(Q3|Q'=6)(8) >= ((4-delta)/16)[log(1/(4 delta (4-delta)))+1], which diverges as delta->0. Thus no universal sup_b ||p_(Q3|Q'=b)||_infinity bound can serve as a general proof interface. Retain the p_(Q')(b) mass weight and aggregate before taking a supremum.
replacement_obligation: Prove a mass-weighted scalar-conditioning or other aggregate-before-supremum estimate rather than a uniform conditional L-infinity cap.
